subject: Accountancy
chapter: Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm – Retirement/Death of a Partner
central_question: How is the amount due to a retiring or deceased partner measured, adjusted and settled while the continuing partners reconstitute the firm?
in_scope_units: Ascertaining the amount due to a retiring partner, including capital, goodwill, reserves, revaluation, current-year profit and drawings.
Calculation of the new profit-sharing ratio and the gaining ratio of continuing partners.
Treatment of goodwill when it does not appear in the books, when it already appears and when its value is hidden.
Revaluation of assets and liabilities and adjustment of accumulated profits and losses in the old ratio.
Disposal of the amount due through immediate payment or a retiring partner’s loan account with interest and instalments.
Adjustment of continuing partners’ capitals according to the new ratio.
Death of a partner, calculation of profit up to the date of death and transfer to the executor’s account.
banned_topics: Admission of a new partner, which belongs to the preceding reconstitution chapter.
Realisation of all assets and closure of the firm, which belongs to dissolution.
Company share capital, debentures and corporate financial statements.
must_include_keywords: profit up to date of death

known_pitfalls.claim: The retiring partner receives only the closing capital balance.
known_pitfalls.correction: The amount due also includes or deducts goodwill, reserves, revaluation, current-year profit, interest, salary, drawings and other agreed items.

known_pitfalls.claim: The gaining ratio is always the old profit-sharing ratio.
known_pitfalls.correction: Gaining ratio is calculated partner-wise as new share minus old share and depends on how the retiring partner’s share is acquired.

known_pitfalls.claim: Revaluation profit is transferred to the continuing partners in their new ratio.
known_pitfalls.correction: It arose before retirement and is shared by all old partners, including the retiring partner, in the old ratio.

known_pitfalls.claim: The deceased partner can share only profit already finalised in accounts.
known_pitfalls.correction: A reasonable share of profit from the last closing date to the date of death is credited according to the deed or an accepted time or sales basis.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Illustrations 1–5 to compute new and gaining ratios.
Use NCERT Illustrations 6–10 to adjust goodwill, including existing and hidden goodwill.
Use NCERT Illustration 11 to prepare the retiring partner’s loan account under instalment alternatives.
Use NCERT Illustrations 12–13 for complete retirement accounts with revaluation and reserves.
Use NCERT Illustrations 14–17 to adjust capitals of continuing partners.
Use NCERT Illustrations 18–19 for death of a partner, current-year profit and executor settlement.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Questions for Practice containing Short Answer, Long Answer and Numerical Questions on retirement, death, gaining ratio, goodwill, revaluation, settlement and capital adjustment.
